diagnostic_evidence.quote: by \Cref{Ass:Potentials} there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that the following inequality holds component-wise

issues.failure_explanation: The cited comparison theorem (Yamada 1973, Theorem 1.3) is a one-dimensional result; it is applied componentwise to d-dimensional SDEs whose bounding drifts \bar b_i(x) = C(1+\|x\|) depend on the whole state through \|x\|. Since \|x\| is not coordinatewise monotone on \R^d, the order condition required by any multidimensional comparison principle (for each coordinate i, -\bar b_i(x) \le -(\partial U(y))_i \le \bar b_i(y) whenever x \le y with x_i = y_i) fails: e.g. for U(z) = (m/2)\|z\|^2 + L z_1 z_2 + K|z_2| with |L| < m (which satisfies Ass:Potentials) one can pick x \le y with x_1 = y_1 and \|x\| \gg \|y\| so that -(\partial U(x))_1 > C(1+\|y\|) = \bar b_1(y). Hence the ordering \tilde X^-_t \le X_t \le \tilde X^+_t is not established, and with it the claim E[sup_{s\le t}\|X_s\|^2] < \infty is unproven as written.

failure_location.quote: By the comparison theorem for stochastic processes \cite[Theorem 1.3]{yamada1973comparison} and using the fact that $(X_t)_{t \geq 0}$ and $(\tilde{X}^\pm_t)_{t \geq 0}$ are strong solutions to their respective SDEs, we can immediately deduce that $\tilde{X}^-_t\leq X_t\leq \tilde{X}^+_t$, for all $t$ component-wise almost surely.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the comparison argument by the standard a priori estimate: apply Ito's formula to \|X_t\|^2 using \langle x, \partial U(x)\rangle \ge m\|x\|^2 \ge 0 and the linear growth of the drift, close via Gronwall for E\|X_t\|^2, and control the supremum with Burkholder-Davis-Gundy. This textbook estimate yields the same bound, after which all downstream proofs stand verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The square-integrability claim E[sup_{s\le t}\|X_s\|^2] < \infty loses its proof. Everything built on finite second moments of the SDE solution inherits the gap: continuity of t -> E\|X_t\|^2 (lemma:continuous_second_moment), the W_2 contraction (lemma:contraction), existence/uniqueness of the stationary law (thm:fixedpoint_SDE) and its identification with pi (thm:identifying_stat_measure).
issues.title: Comparison theorem misapplied componentwise to d-dimensional SDEs in the second-moment bound
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is true and the repair is a short, local, routine textbook bypass (Ito-Gronwall-BDG) that preserves every substantive claim, guarantee and rate with no new nontrivial lemma or change of architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the last inequality holds for $\tau$ sufficiently small.

issues.failure_explanation: The statement contains no step-size restriction, i.e. it claims geometric ergodicity for every tau > 0, but the drift estimate (eq:ergodic1) is only valid 'for tau sufficiently small' (tau \le m/c). The unrestricted claim is false: with d = 1 and U(x) = (L/2)x^2, which satisfies Ass:Potentials with m = L, the scheme reads X_{k+1} = (1 - tau L)X_k + sqrt(2 tau)W_k; for tau > 2/L this AR(1) recursion satisfies |1 - tau L| > 1, is transient and admits no stationary distribution pi^tau, so the chain is not geometrically ergodic. The proposition, and the LLN that presupposes pi^tau, hold only for sufficiently small tau.

failure_location.quote: The Markov chain $(X^\tau_k)_{k \in \N}$ from \eqref{eq:explicit_scheme} with $X_0^\tau=x_0\in\R^d$ arbitrary is geometrically ergodic.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the statement to step sizes tau in (0, bar tau] for some sufficiently small bar tau > 0 (and likewise prop:LLN_explicit); the given proof and every application (fixed small step size and tau -> 0 asymptotics) are unaffected.
issues.overall_effect: Geometric ergodicity of the explicit scheme and the law of large numbers of prop:LLN_explicit are unsupported, and in fact false as stated, for large step sizes; only a small-tau version survives.
issues.title: Explicit-scheme geometric ergodicity stated for all step sizes but proved (and true) only for small tau
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard small-step-size hypothesis is a one-clause local condition; the method, conclusion, rate, and the advertised fixed-step-size scope all survive, so the repair is minor.

issues.failure_explanation: Two linked defects. (i) The statement claims geometric ergodicity for every constant step size tau > 0; this is false for large tau: with G identically 0 (admissible under Ass:F_G) and F(x) = (L/2)x^2 in d = 1, the scheme is X_{k+1} = (1 - tau L)X_k + sqrt(2 tau)W_k, which has no stationary distribution for tau > 2/L. (ii) Even within the proof the step-size condition is misstated: the final bound (1 - tau mL/(m+L))\|X-Y\|^2 requires discarding (tau^2 - tau/(m+L))\|nabla F(X) - nabla F(Y)\|^2, which needs tau \le 1/(m+L), not the stated tau^2 < 1/(m+L); e.g. m = 1, L = 8, tau = 0.3 satisfies tau^2 < 1/(m+L), yet in the L-eigendirection the one-step map expands by |1 - tau L| = 1.4 while the claimed squared contraction factor is 1 - tau mL/(m+L) = 0.73.

failure_location.quote: The proximal-gradient scheme with constant step size $\tau>0$ is geometrically ergodic with respect to the Wasserstein-2 distance

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the result for tau in (0, 1/(m+L)] (or tau \le 2/(m+L) using the sharp co-coercivity constant) and correct the condition in the proof accordingly; all downstream results, which concern fixed small tau or tau -> 0, are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Geometric ergodicity of the semi-implicit scheme and its law of large numbers (prop:added-1) are established only for sufficiently small tau; the universal statement is false for large tau, and the claimed contraction factor is not valid on the range written in the proof.
issues.title: Semi-implicit contraction stated for all tau>0 and proved under a misstated step-size condition
issues.why_classification: The repair is a corrected, standard step-size restriction applied locally; the conclusion, the contraction-based rate, and the paper's small-tau applications all survive intact.

issues.failure_explanation: The recursion is driven by the per-step estimate \|x - tau nabla F(x)\| \le (1 - tau mL/(m+L))^{1/2}\|x\| + tau\|nabla F(0)\|, which comes from dropping the non-positive term tau(tau - 2/(m+L))\|nabla F(x) - nabla F(0)\|^2 and is therefore valid only for tau \le 2/(m+L). The proof fixes tau_max := (m+L)/(2mL), which is strictly larger than 2/(m+L) whenever m \ne L (AM-GM). On the excess range the estimate fails: for F(x) = (L x_1^2 + m x_2^2)/2 and x = (t,0), at tau = tau_max one has \|x - tau nabla F(x)\| = (L-m)/(2m) \|x\|, which exceeds the claimed factor (1 - tau mL/(m+L))^{1/2}\|x\| = 2^{-1/2}\|x\| whenever L > (1+sqrt 2)m. Hence the moment recursion that drives the whole proof is unjustified (indeed false as stated) on part of the interval [0, tau_max].

failure_location.quote: In the following, we fix $\tau \leq \tau_{\text{max}} := \frac{1}{2} \frac{m + L}{m L}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reduce the range to tau_max = min{2/(m+L), (m+L)/(2mL)} = 2/(m+L); the remainder of the proof is verbatim and yields the same statement.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform second-moment bound is not proven on the full range [0, (m+L)/(2mL)] as claimed; the existential statement itself, and its use in prop:implicit_final_convergence (only tau -> 0 matters there), survive once the range is reduced.
issues.title: Moment-bound lemma uses the gradient contraction outside its valid step-size range
issues.why_classification: The statement is existential, so a single forced parameter reduction restores it with every conclusion and downstream use preserved; the repair is routine and local.
